Despite Mac shipments falling 11% in Q3 2026, Apple's market share actually rose from 8.5% to 9.5% as the overall market shipments dropped sharply by 20.1%, according to the latest IDC report. Full details below.

Apple outperforms most of the PC market amid challenging conditions

IDC today released its global PC shipment report for Q3 2026, noting that while Apple's Mac shipments declined year-on-year, its performance was clearly better than the overall market.

According to IDC's preliminary figures, Apple shipped 5.9 million Macs in Q3 2026, down 11.3% from 6.7 million in the same quarter last year.

However, the overall PC market saw a more pronounced decline, with global shipments falling 20.1% year-on-year to 62.7 million units.

As a result, Apple's share of global PC shipments actually rose from 8.5% to 9.5%.

Apple remained in fourth place, behind Lenovo, HP and Dell. Lenovo took the top spot with 14.9 million units shipped and a 23.8% market share, followed by HP with 10.3 million units and a 16.5% share, while Dell came third with 7.6 million units and a 12.1% share.

Among the top five vendors, HP posted the steepest year-on-year decline, with shipments falling 30.9%. ASUS recorded the smallest drop, down 8.6% year-on-year, shipping 5.5 million units for an 8.7% market share.

IDC said:

Looking ahead, IDC noted that "channel concerns over high inventory and weak demand at high prices could trigger promotional activities in the near term," adding that "prices will remain well above the levels seen a year ago."

The firm also said economic conditions had weakened since the previous quarter, further hurting demand and making "the outlook for the remainder of 2026 and 2027 dimmer."
